rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE USE OF PURCHASE ORDERS AND NOT MERELY OF QUEDAN OR WAREHOUSE RECEIPTS AS COLLATERALS FOR OBTAINING CREDIT FINANCING, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-THREE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE QUEDAN AND RURAL CREDIT GUARANTEE CORPORATION ACT
rows.abstract: Rationale: Under existing law (RA 7393), only queden or warehouse receipt evidencing stored agri-aqua produce in bonded warehouses may be used as collaterals for obtaining credit financing subject to a guarantee by the Quedan and Credit Guarantee Corporation created under said law.  It is felt however, that forward selling schemes as advanced in Asian developed countries, should be set up in order to enhance agricultural production especially in the countrysides. Hence, the use of purchase orders as collaterals for obtaining credit financing. Seeks to reassure income to small farmers and fishermen, as well as to guarantee repayment of loans.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 1996-11-18

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE JUVENILE JUSTICE SYSTEM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "Comprehensive Juvenile Justice System Law of 1996" Declares it the policy of the State to undertake a COMPREHENSIVE REFORM in its system of administering JUVENILE JUSTICE by adopting the minimum standards accepted by the United Nations consisted with human rights and fundamental freedoms. Provides for these areas of concern: (1) Investigation of youth offender; (2) Filing of charges before the juvenile court; (3) Release on recognizance; (4) Detention of youth offender; pre-trial determination; (5) Suspension of sentence and commitment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1996-11-18

rows.abstract: Proposes the following amendment to Section 265 of the Omnibus Election Code" "SECTION 265. Prosecution. The Commission, shall through its duly authorized legal officers, MOTU PROPIO, UPON KNOWLEDGE OF A POSSIBLE ELECTION OFFENSE OR UPON COMPLAINT FILED BY A PARTY, have the exclusive power to conduct preliminary investigation of all election offenders ... and to prosecute the same WITHIN DELAY. x x x That UPON THE CONCLUSION OF THE PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATION, AND THERE BE A PROBABLE CAUSE, THE COMMISSION SHALL TRANSMIT WITHIN THIRTY DAYS TO THE PROPER COURT HAVING JURISDICTION OF THE OFFENSE, ALL RECORDS OF THE CASE FOR PROPER INVESTIGATION AND PROSECUTION, IF WARRANTED. PERTINENT PROVISIONS OF THE RULES OF COURT WILL HAVE SUPPLETORY EFFECTT ON THE PROCEDURES NOT HEREWITH ENUMERATED. Section 2. ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS - FAILURE OF THE CONCERNED OFFICIALS AND PERSONNEL TO IMMEDIATELY ACT ON ELECTION OFFENSES SHALL BE CONSIDERED GROSS NEGLECT OF DUTY AND SHALL HAVE CORRESPONDING ADMINIS

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING SEPTEMBER THIRTEEN OF EVERY YEAR AS "BATTLE OF PULANG LUPA DAY" AND A SPECIAL NON-WORKING NATIONAL HOLIDAY
rows.abstract: Rationale: September 13, 1898 is a day of victory for our Filipino forebears in their quest for independence from foreign domination. Our countrymen showed their patriotism when they revolted against the Americans who rules the Province of Marinduque. To commemorate said historical event, September 13 of every year was declared as Battle of Pulang Lupa Day and a special non-working holiday in the Province of Marinduque under Republic Act No. 6702. Viewed on a national perspective, the Battle ofPulang Lupa did not only benefit the people of Marinduque but all of the Filipinos in our quest for genuine independence.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1996-11-18

rows.author: B051
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE INCLUSION OF ENTREPRENEURSHI P AS A SEPARATE SUBJECT IN THE HIGH SCHOOL CURRICULUM
rows.abstract: Rationale: Entrepreneurshi p has become one of the favorite among development planners in the country today.  And for a good reason, too: the contributions of entreprenuers to the growth of our economy have made them indispensable components of ourdevelopment efforts. Hence, sustaining development in the ocuntry, with the end in view of attaining our industrializati on goals, requires the proper education and training of entrepreneurs. And this education and training must be done while they are young. Children must, therefore, be introduced to and acquainted with the exciting and empowering field of entrepreneurshi p. States that there shall be a separate subject on entrepreneurshi p in the SENIOR YEAR CURRICULUM of both public and privatte secodnary schools nationwide. Proposes the inclusion  of the following entrepreneurial subject matters: (1) Management; (2) funds sourcing; (3) program accreditation requirements; and (4) contemporary entrepreneurial practices.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING HAZARD PAY TO ALL DULY-APPOINTED MEMBERS OF BARANGAY TANOD BRIGADES DURING THEIR INCUMBENCY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Barangay tanod brigades were organized to assist the government in the maintenance of peace and order in the country. Pursuant  to such duty, they conduct rondas or nightly patrols, necessarily , exposing their lives and limbs to danger in the hands of criminal elements and other wayward members of society.  In fact, an alarming number of barangay tanods have already been assaulted, injured and/or killed, leaving their families and dependents to fend for themselves. Provides for thefollowing --- " SECTION 1. All duly-appointed barangay tanods shall be granted a hazard pay, during their incumbency, in the amount of Two Hundred Pesos (P200.00) per month."

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION THIRTY-FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTEEN OF THE TARIFF AND CUSTOMS CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Tariff and Customs Code of the Philippines provides that a cash reward be given to a person who is instrumental in the discovery and seizure of smuggled goods even if such informer is a government official or employee. However, the system has opened the door to government officials and employees who use their positions to entrap violators and them claim for such reward. the reward should only be given if the informer is a private individual and not a government official or employee, who are in fact under obligation to eprform the act of being the subject of a reward. Provides, therefore for the following --- :Sec. 3513. Reward to persons instrumental in the Discovery and Seizure of Smuggled Goods.- The provisions of generaland special laws to the contrary notwithstanding ,  a cash reward equivalent to [twenty] FIFTEEN per centum [20] 15 of the fair market value of the smuggled and confiscated goods shall be given to the [officers and men and] informers who are isntrume

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE START OF THE SCHOOL YEAR ON THE FIRST MONDAY OF SEPTEMBER AND SHALL END UP TO THE MONTH OF JUNE BUT NOT EXCEEDING TWO HUNDRED TWENTY (220) CLASS DAYS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7797
rows.abstract: Rationale: The months of June until August fall under the rainy season. The primary reason for this is that the months of June until August would fall on the rainy season. Hence, not only are the students inconvenienced by the bad weather in attending their classes but suspension of classes are rather expected due to typhoons especially in flood-prone areas. Teachers, therefore, tend to cram their lessons and the students end up with half-baked learning. "Section 1. Section three of Republic Act No. 7797 is hereby amended to read as follows: Section 3. Start of the School Year.- The school year shall start on the first Monday of [June] SPETEMBER but not later than the last day of [August] NOVEMBER. >In the implementation of this Act, the SSecretary of Education, Culture and Sports shall determine the EXACT DATE of the end of the regular school year AND WHICH SHOULD FALL ON THE MONTH OF JUNE, taking into consideration the Christmas and [summer] vacations, and the peculiar circumstances

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COMMISSION ON ELECTIONS TO USE AN AUTOMATED ELECTION SYSTEM NATIONWIDE IN THE MAY 11, 1998 NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS AND IN OTHER NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS THEREAFTER, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: With the employment of mdoern technologies in the counting and canvassing of votes, the perennial problem and vicious cycle of electoral fraud which has now come to be known as operation "dagdag-bawas" shall be addressed. For one, it shall eliminate human intervention in the reading of ballots and in the accomplishment of election returns, as well as tremendously shorten the period in determining the votes for every elective position whicha re usually the areas where fraud takes place.> Proposes the use of electronic devices in the country and canvassing of votes during the May 11, 1998 elections.
